scores.name: Happy-on-Tailnet
scores.breakdown: Pain end-to-end 24/30 (all functional wants covered same-day, but 'single remote' is split across Happy + VibeTunnel/Blink, and Phases 2-3 depend on a hosted relay with documented outages); Buildable/maintainable 22/25 (near-zero custom code, maintenance = config + launchd plists; deduction for inheriting Happy's fix latency and the Omnara-style upstream treadmill); UX ceiling 14/20 (Happy's inbox/streaming/handoff are already polished, but the ceiling is capped at what upstream ships and the two-app split hurts the unified experience); Security 12/15 (tailnet-only, E2E, no public ports — but interim hosted relay + unaudited Happy crypto with #680 history until Phase 4); Extensibility 7/10 (Codex/ACP agents ride free, but bounded by upstream; in-app terminals require a fork); Over-engineering penalty 0 — this is the anti-over-engineering design, and its only real code (Phase 5) is explicitly deferred.

scores.name: Tether
scores.breakdown: Pain end-to-end 27/30 (genuinely single app, agents + terminals + IDE in one, but ~18 days before full coverage and load-bearing UNVERIFIED assumptions); Buildable/maintainable 14/25 (squarely in the user's TS/Expo stack, but one person owns a daemon, a mobile app, and a VS Code extension forever, against SDK churn, ACP immaturity, TestFlight 90-day expiry, and $99/yr); UX ceiling 18/20 (fully custom: FlashList streams, lock-screen actions, honest capability labels — highest polish ceiling); Security 14/15 (WireGuard-direct, typed ops only, hashed revocable tokens, audit log, allowlisted roots); Extensibility 8/10 (ACP tier makes future agents adapter work); raw 81, over-engineering penalty -7 for rebuilding ~90% of a maintained MIT project to serve one user.

scores.name: Switchboard
scores.breakdown: Pain end-to-end 27/30 (same single-app coverage as Tether with slightly better phase ordering — remote start before terminals); Buildable/maintainable 14/25 (same three-artifact forever-maintenance burden, 16 days, plus a formal internal wire protocol as extra conceptual surface); UX ceiling 18/20 (capability badges, four option kinds, five purpose-built screens); Security 14/15 (identical Tailscale-direct posture, Face ID + revocation explicitly shipped in Phase 1); Extensibility 9/10 (best on paper: agents.toml config entry, dumb client rendered from capability flags); raw 82, over-engineering penalty -9 — 'the product IS the protocol' is exactly the build-for-hypothetical-futures pattern the user rejects, and its own risks section concedes it rebuilds ~90% of Happy for protocol purity.

rationale: The user's own stated rule — build what's needed, not what might be needed — plus the 25-point maintainability axis is decisive. All three designs solve the core pain (approvals from the phone, streaming, remote start, terminal control); the differentiator is cost of ownership. Happy-on-Tailnet delivers a working approvals inbox with push the same day and full coverage in about a week of configuration, with essentially zero code for one person to maintain; the store-distributed Happy app also deletes the single largest hidden cost of the custom designs, the $99/yr Apple program plus TestFlight 90-day re-upload treadmill for a one-user app. Tether and Switchboard have a higher UX ceiling and a marginally cleaner security story (no third-party relay ever), but both concede in their own risk sections that they rebuild ~90% of a maintained 22.9k-star MIT project — that is precisely the over-engineering the brief penalizes, and Omnara's deprecation shows how solo-maintained agent wrappers end. Happy-on-Tailnet's real weaknesses — hosted-relay dependence until Phase 4, the two-app agents/terminals split, unverified load-bearing assumptions, and zero laptop-outage detection — are all addressable by grafts below without changing its glue-first character, and its bounded exit (Phase 5 fork of Happy's Expo app) means the single-app requirement is deferred, not abandoned. Standalone-app requirement is met: Happy is a native store app, not a mobile web page.
grafts: Switchboard's day-one verification spikes: pull all three UNVERIFIED load-bearing items (killed-state notification actions on real devices, self-hosted push delivery through the store apps, Happy's lack of plain-terminal sessions) into Phase 1-2 as explicit spikes instead of deferring each to the phase that depends on it — the plan's shape changes if any fails, so verify before building on them.

Tether/Switchboard's zero-third-party transport stance applied as phase reordering: move Phase 4 (self-hosted happy-server behind tailscale serve) to immediately after Phase 2, because the hosted relay's documented outages and the #680 key-custody history make it the weakest reliability and security link, and self-hosting costs only ~1.5 days.

Switchboard's heartbeat risk mitigation: add a tiny launchd health-check that alerts the phone when the laptop goes unreachable (dead-man's-switch style), since the winner names laptop sleep/power/ISP as the most likely real outage but ships zero detection for it — this is the one piece of custom glue code worth writing early.

Switchboard's tmux no-resize invariant codified as configuration, not habit: set an explicit window-size policy in .tmux.conf and never view agent TUIs through a phone-attached tmux client (Happy only), because Claude Code's ink TUI demonstrably corrupts on resize and the winner currently carries this only as a risk note.

Tether's exclusive single-writer attach discipline: treat every Claude session as owned by exactly one driver (happy daemon or laptop CLI) with an explicit release-then-resume handoff, never concurrent `claude --resume` of the same session ID, since dual-writer JSONL behavior is unverified and transcript corruption is the failure mode.

Adopt the losing designs' terminal-adapter specs as the ready-made Phase 5 blueprint: if the two-app UX fails, build the Happy fork's terminal session type directly from Switchboard's TmuxAdapter spec (capture-pane -p -e -S - replay, %output octal-unescape, pause-after flow control, @xterm/headless serialize snapshots) plus Tether's xterm.js-WebView write-coalescing and laptop-side-size rendering — converting the winner's riskiest phase from design work into a follow-the-spec build.

Tether's allowlisted-project-roots-by-API-shape control for remote spawn: if the Phase 5 fork ever happens (or if happy-cli grows the config hook), constrain phone-initiated session starts to configured roots so remote code execution is bounded by API shape rather than trust in the paired device alone.
